title: Tax Unit Certification Standard: Employer Account Standing and the Reopened Hearing Window (Unemployment Insurance Appeals)
content:
Before a reopened hearing on an employer's appeal under Unemployment Insurance Appeals the tax unit certifies the employer's account to the hearing officer, and an account that is paid up and reporting is certified without a review, so its reopened hearing is set on a shorter window. The standing of the account is read from the employer's Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts records: the payments recorded as received on the account and the quarterly contribution and wage reports with their filing and due dates.

**Standard.** The reopened-setting window — the number of calendar days after the day the reopened-setting clock starts on which the reopened hearing date falls — is the current-account window days for an employer appellant whose tax account recorded payments received of at least the paid-contribution floor in the three months before today and whose latest quarterly contribution and wage report was filed on or before its due date; it is the paying-account window days for an employer appellant whose tax account recorded payments received of at least the paid-contribution floor in those three months and whose latest quarterly report was filed after its due date; and it is the docket's reschedule window days for an employer appellant meeting neither condition and for a claimant appellant. Payments received are the payments recorded as received on the account; voluntary contributions are not payments received for this purpose. The three months before today cover the dates later than the same day of the month three months before today, up to and including today.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Paid-contribution floor (total payments received in the three months) | $2500.00 |
| Current-account window | 10 calendar days |
| Paying-account window | 17 calendar days |

## Window by account standing

| Appellant | Payments received in the three months total at least $2500.00 | Latest quarterly report | Reopened-setting window |
|---|---|---|---|
| employer | yes | filed on or before its due date | 10 days |
| employer | yes | filed after its due date | 17 days |
| employer | yes | none on file | the docket's reschedule window |
| employer | no | any | the docket's reschedule window |
| claimant | — | — | the docket's reschedule window |

The docket's reschedule window days are: Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue 14; Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue 14; Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination 14; Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud 14; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge 21; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate 21; Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review 0.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical account; today is Wednesday 15 April 2026)

- *The three months.* The same day three months before is 15 January; the three months cover 16 January through 15 April, both included.
- *Reaching the floor.* Payments received of $1800.00 on 20 January and $700.00 on 14 April total exactly $2500.00, which is at least the floor. A payment received on 15 January falls outside the three months and is not counted.
- *Voluntary contributions.* A voluntary contribution booked on the account in the three months is not a payment received and adds nothing toward the floor.
- *Latest report.* The report read is the one for the latest quarter. If it was filed on its due date it counts as on or before the due date; filed a day later, it is after its due date.
- *Below the floor.* An employer whose payments received in the three months total $2499.00 takes the docket's reschedule window — 21 days on the Employer Benefit Charge docket — whatever its reporting record.
